name: Browny Orange
lede: Browny Orange is a warm, burnt-looking orange, a plain-spoken name for the color between orange and brown.

sections.title: The name
sections.body:
The name comes from the xkcd color survey, where people named colors on screen, and the swatch sits near [[ochre]] [1]. It is a descriptive name with no pigment behind it [1].

Paterson's dictionary uses the same words to define oriole, a browny orange colour, after the bird [3]. That is a gloss, not an origin for this swatch [3]. Its lightness and chroma put it among the brighter, more saturated members of the orange family rather than the muted browns [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Browny Orange appears in 0.49% of the 23,781 paintings in our archive, as photographed [2]. It peaks in the 1900s at 0.9% of that century's paintings, 1.7 times the baseline [2]. Inside a painting it most often plays an accent, in 81% of cases [2]. It is most over-represented in Indian paintings, at 3.6 times expected [2]. These are photographs, so aged varnish moves the result [2].
